title: JPMorgan resets Amazon stock target after AI payoff
excerpt: Amazon (AMZN) stock blasted off post-earnings as Wall Street celebrated evidence that its whopping artificial intelligence (AI) spending was producing a meas...
content_html:
Amazon (AMZN) stock blasted off post-earnings as Wall Street celebrated evidence that its whopping artificial intelligence (AI) spending was producing a measurable payoff. 

For the most part, investors were bracing for another quarter marred by fears of capital expenditure and questions about whether AWS could grow quickly enough to justify the buildout. 

Instead, cloud sales rose sharply, operating profit expanded, and backlog climbed to a record level.

On the flip side, as I reported on Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon's cash flow deteriorated as infrastructure spending soared. 

However, backed into a corner, Amazon delivered its strongest growth numbers in years.

That shift led JPMorgan to reassess the stock's earnings power and the durability of its AI investment cycle. 

At the heart of the reset is a question of whether AWS can convert booming demand into sufficient long-term profit to outweigh Amazon's severe near-term cash burn.

Why JPMorgan sees an AWS inflection, not just an earnings beat 

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth bumped Amazon's price target to $365 from $330, retaining an Overweight rating and keeping the stock in his Best Idea list. 

For context, that is nearly a 34.4% upside from current prices.

The bank's thesis centered on Amazon's breathtaking top-line growth.

More AI:

  • Workers just sent AI companies an ultimatum

  • Palantir CEO has a blunt verdict on OpenAI and Anthropic

  • Elon Musk pulls no punches with AI rivals as Grok 4.5 debuts

Amazon's overall sales were up 20%, its fastest growth in 20 quarters, while its cloud behemoth AWS grew 37%, its fastest rate in 18 quarters. 

More importantly, AWS backlog reached $496 billion, rising 36% sequentially and nearly 2.5 times year over year, offering investors a ton of visibility into future cloud sales.

On top of that, AWS's AI and custom-chip businesses, spearheaded by its Graviton CPU, posted an eye-catching $25 billion annual sales run rate. Growing at a triple-digit clip.

Additionally, AWS's operating income surged 64% to $16.6 billion, while its operating margin expanded to 39.4%. Hence, AWS carried nearly 61% of Amazon's consolidated operating profit, despite accounting for one-fifth of revenue.

Related: Amazon earnings verdict has major blind spot

For perspective, though, AWS's 37% growth was the slowest among the cloud czars, trailing Microsoft Azure and other cloud services at 43% and Google Cloud at 82%.  

Consequently, Anmuth and his team argue that Amazon is showing concrete evidence of booming AI demand rather than simply making promises.

content_html_zh:
亚马逊 (AMZN) 股价在财报发布后大幅上涨，华尔街庆祝有证据表明其庞大的人工智能 (AI) 支出正在产生可衡量的回报。

在大多数情况下，投资者都在为下一个季度做好准备，因为他们担心资本支出，并质疑 AWS 能否快速增长以证明扩建的合理性。

相反，云销售额大幅增长，营业利润扩大，积压订单攀升至创纪录水平。

另一方面，正如我在 Alphabet (GOOGL) 上报道的那样，随着基础设施支出飙升，亚马逊的现金流恶化。

然而，陷入困境的亚马逊却实现了多年来最强劲的增长数据。

这一转变导致摩根大通重新评估该股的盈利能力及其人工智能投资周期的持久性。

此次重置的核心问题是，AWS 能否将蓬勃发展的需求转化为足够的长期利润，以抵消亚马逊近期严重的现金消耗。

为什么摩根大通看到 AWS 出现拐点，而不仅仅是盈利好转

摩根大通分析师道格·安穆斯 (Doug Anmuth) 将亚马逊的目标股价从 330 美元上调至 365 美元，维持“增持”评级，并将该股保留在他的“最佳创意”名单中。

就背景而言，这比当前价格上涨了近 34.4%。

该银行的论文集中于亚马逊惊人的营收增长。

更多人工智能：

  • 工人们刚刚向人工智能公司发出最后通牒
  • Palantir 首席执行官对 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 做出了直率的判断
  • Grok 4.5 首次亮相，埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 对人工智能竞争对手不遗余力

亚马逊的整体销售额增长了 20%，是 20 个季度以来的最快增长，而其云巨头 AWS 增长了 37%，是 18 个季度以来的最快增速。

更重要的是，AWS 积压订单达到 4960 亿美元，环比增长 36%，同比增长近 2.5 倍，为投资者提供了对未来云销售的大量了解。

除此之外，以 Graviton CPU 为首的 AWS 人工智能和定制芯片业务的年销售额达到了令人瞩目的 250 亿美元。 以三位数的速度增长。

此外，AWS 的营业收入飙升 64% 至 166 亿美元，营业利润率扩大至 39.4%。 因此，尽管 AWS 占亚马逊营收的五分之一，但它却占据了亚马逊综合运营利润的近 61%。

相关：亚马逊盈利判断存在重大盲点

不过，从长远来看，AWS 37% 的增长是云沙皇中最慢的，落后于微软 Azure 和其他云服务的 43%，以及谷歌云的 82%。

因此，安姆斯和他的团队认为，亚马逊正在展示人工智能需求蓬勃发展的具体证据，而不是简单地做出承诺。
